Chief_Complaint.content: Patient presents with swelling of the upper lip.
Chief_Complaint.source_text: Uh, now I feel the that there is a swelling, there is like a swelling on my, on my upper lip and it's kind of getting bigger.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Symptoms began after eating prawn soup.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Um, so what happened was, I, I ordered a prawn soup it it's it it's called it's like a soup, I ordered a prawn one this time.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Initial lip symptoms started at the left corner.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: And, yeah and then my feel like my lips started feeling a little weird just in the in the corner sort of on the left first.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Upper lip swelling is increasing in size.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Uh, now I feel the that there is a swelling, there is like a swelling on my, on my upper lip and it's kind of getting bigger.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Swelling developed approximately 30 minutes after eating.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Well I wasn't really paying attention so, it must have been like, must have been like, I don't know half an hour maybe.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient reports worsening sensation with throbbing and progressive enlargement.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Yeah it's it it still feel it like, really pumping blood and it's kinda getting bigger it feels like it's getting worse.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient feels she cannot breathe well.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Yeah actually, I, I feel like I can't breathe that well right now.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient reports general breathing difficulty and is unsure about chest tightness.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: And do you feel like, like your chest is tight? And I don't know if it's the chest it just generally feels a little difficult, but yeah it might be, I'm not sure.
Ohh, I feel a little dizzy right now to be honest, ohh.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Prawn soup was consumed at approximately 7 PM after work.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: That was, that must have been just after work, so maybe like around seven.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient does not have antihistamines on hand at the time of initial questioning.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: No, I don't think I have no.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient had a similar episode about a year ago.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Yeah, well, maybe, I remember like a year ago.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: During the prior episode, she awoke very swollen with difficulty breathing after eating late-night food.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: I've woke up the next morning quite swollen up and had also I, felt really bad and quite difficult breathing, but I don't know what it was I had it was like a curry or something I think.

Medications.source_text: But I generally have asthma so, I took I, I take, ohh what's it called? Salbutamol inhalers?

Medications.content: Patient is not using any other inhalers besides salbutamol.
Medications.source_text: Ohh I, no I don't think so, no.

Medications.content: Patient sometimes takes antihistamines but is unsure which ones.
Medications.source_text: I, think I do get antihistamines for that but I'm not sure which ones.

Adverse_Drug_Reactions_and_Allergies.source_text: I have a peanut allergy as well, like always had it.

Adverse_Drug_Reactions_and_Allergies.content: As a child, the patient reportedly received an injection for an allergic reaction; details unknown.
Adverse_Drug_Reactions_and_Allergies.source_text: And any point because you had peanut allergy, any time you have to ever use like an injection? When I was a kid I think I remember my mom told me about it, but I don't know what it was 'cause I was small and I've changed doctors since.

Assessment.source_text: It sounds like you could be going into what we say an a, an anaphylactic reaction.

Plan_of_Care.content: Call an ambulance immediately for suspected anaphylaxis.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Right, uh, all right I, I'm really a bit worried about you at the moment, Maria. Um I think we need to call an ambulance, because, um, from what history you've been telling me. It sounds like you could be going into what we say an a, an anaphylactic reaction.

Plan_of_Care.content: Ensure someone stays with the patient until the ambulance arrives.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: So just call the ambulance make sure that person's with you till the ambulance comes, yeah.

Plan_of_Care.content: Mother to call 999 and report suspected anaphylactic reaction requiring urgent response.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Mum, if you can call the uh nine nine , nine nine nine yeah, and say that your there is a suspected anaphylactic reaction and they need to come straight away. OK.

Plan_of_Care.content: Take an antihistamine immediately while waiting for the ambulance.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: All right, so straight away take the antihistamines in the meantime all right.

Plan_of_Care.content: After hospital treatment, arrange further management that may include injections.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: And after you come out from the hospital do give us a ring back we might need to sort you out, um, with your injections and things like that OK?

Follow_up_Information.content: Patient to call the clinic after discharge from hospital.
Follow_up_Information.source_text: And after you come out from the hospital do give us a ring back
